Community and Website

We need to focus on better quality.

Hare and I are going to discuss potential new temporary rules to encourage quality content but I encourage people to want to submit awesomeness. One problem w/ contests, and why I used to do them quantity-based, is that the voting system has been a bad measurement of quality in the past. On the other hand, quantity-based contests promote lower quality. We'll need to be creative in how to best do this moving forward on this platform and for now I am going to have others around me discuss and pick winners until I work out a more transparent / better way.

Plainly, this startup is absolutely not guaranteed to end up surviving. If you like this community, the previous community (what it was), or believe in its future / concept - please consider helping me improve it. It'd mean a lot to me and I want to keep the fun going & growing. The website has progressed and we will be moving towards an alpha release ahead of schedule! I'm human

I just wanted to touch on my likely perceived lack of involvement here. Basically, I'm human with a constrained amount of hours and emotional capacity. This year started off fantastic and then crashed to become one of the biggest professional and personal obstacles I've ever had to overcome.

I care a lot about all of you and have been focusing my attention as much as possible on building what we need to welcome the future but to be completely honest - I have had to re-motivate and focus myself several times since I've often felt burdened by the stress of the unknown. I've come out of that cycle this month and will continue to work harder and harder to ensure our new lofty goal's success. If shit hadn't hit the fan in late-January, I likely would have been able to hire a couple people to help, as I planned on doing, but all of my money is being put on the table for this new mockup community to succeed and contests like these.

That said, we are going to come swinging. Our website / subreddit always had swings of hype, ups/downs, and what-not which many (besides probably Haredeenee) won't remember. I'm curious where the markets for bitcoin and gold will intersect. Gold has largely been seen as a sort of hedge against the failure of fiat currency for historical reasons. Its actual material uses are very limited. Like Warren Buffet put it I think aliens watching us would find it most peculiar to see us dig this shiny rock out of the ground, form it into bricks and immediately put it back in the ground and have men with guns walk around guarding it to no apparent end. Bitcoin has a similar purpose with the major difference that it's already being actively used as a fiat alternative and is practical when used as a currency. Gold will always, at best, be some sort of backing to another currency since it's impractical to directly trade for goods and services.

There is a lot more accessible gold than weve thought, but it is in smaller amounts. My dad is a geophysicist who found some interesting principles for finding it, but nowadays gold is a lot like diamonds, controlling the current supply is more important than expansion of the base, so it fell on deaf ears.
I'm happy about this. This is just the push humanity needs for a real large-scale campaign of off-planet travel technology that will allow us to mine asteroids in SPAAAAAAAAAAACE!!!!!!

I imagine "peak gold" would drive up the value, but what happens when we start mining asteroids and we have more gold than we can store? This is one of the reasons bitcoin interests me - it could be viable space money.
